text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive nature of the pain worsening with activity and affecting weight-bearing joints, this presentation is highly suggestive of osteoarthritis. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity of joint degeneration, I need to visualize the joint spaces. REQUEST TEST: X-ray of knees and hips

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hip_and_Knee_X_Rays: Joint space narrowing with osteophyte formation, suggestive of osteoarthritis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of joint space narrowing and osteophytes confirm osteoarthritis, which explains your hip and knee pain. However, the involvement of the left great toe is atypical for pure osteoarthritis and raises suspicion for gout or another inflammatory arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis with suspected concurrent gout
